one_line: Interactive BATS scores and company/sector visualizations for S&P 500 AI transformation analysis.
what_it_does: Combines a catalog of AI-transformation scores with gallery charts, in-browser DuckDB SQL, company reports, and WebMCP-driven query/visualization workflows.
leverage_rationale: Structured query and chart tools reduce the friction of asking cross-company or sector questions compared with manually filtering a catalog, but the underlying analysis remains possible through ordinary UI or exports.
leverage_evidence: About text describes DuckDB ad-hoc SQL and WebMCP agent control of the query surface.
Frame sheet shows a BATS Visualization ranked bar-chart interface.
execution_rationale: The packet presents a coherent visualization product with multiple views and a live demo link; evidence is mostly description plus chart frames and does not prove every end-to-end path.
execution_evidence: FACTS reports a live demo and 13 gallery images.
Frame sheet visibly shows a populated ranked chart UI.
About text enumerates gallery, SQL, company report, heatmap, radar, and sector views.
impact_rationale: The target audience of analysts and researchers has a clear need to compare AI-transformation signals across companies and sectors, and the product directly supports those questions.
impact_evidence: About text gives concrete queries such as healthcare averages and industrials ranked by hype.
Company and sector score views are described.
creativity_rationale: A specialized score dataset is turned into a query-and-chart exploration surface with agent access; this is a fresh synthesis though still within analytics conventions.
creativity_evidence: BATS is framed as a 0–100 rubric with fifteen dimensions.
The product combines fixed chart gallery, SQL, and agent-driven visualization.
usability_note: Multiple views and direct ticker/report navigation suggest good usability; no direct interaction testing was available.
red_flags: No submitted video or transcript; agent invocation is not visibly demonstrated.
standouts: Strong domain-specific analytical surface with both SQL and visual exploration.
advance_reason: Clear, credible analytics product with meaningful structured-query value and visible working UI.

one_line: Evidence-first platform for discovering, verifying, and comparing civic and political data.
what_it_does: Assembles political dossiers from public records and exposes natural-language research operations to AI agents through WebMCP.
leverage_rationale: Civic research spanning heterogeneous records benefits substantially from structured discovery, retrieval, verification, and comparison tools rather than brittle UI navigation.
leverage_evidence: Pitch explicitly centers WebMCP agent discovery, verification, and comparison.
About text lists dossiers combining parliamentary activity, statements, affidavits, assets, and legal records.
execution_rationale: The submission is coherent and packaged as a civic research platform, but no actual application frame or submitted video is provided, so end-to-end completion remains unverified.
execution_evidence: Devpost screenshot visibly presents the project and a demo/presentation preview.
FACTS report a live demo and public repository.
No frame sheets or transcript submitted.
impact_rationale: The audience and problem are specific: researchers and citizens need trustworthy access to fragmented public political records. Evidence-first dossiers and comparisons directly address that need.
impact_evidence: About text identifies fragmented public information as the problem.
Concrete tasks include finding dossiers and retrieving civic/parliamentary information.
creativity_rationale: Applying agent-native evidence handling to civic dossiers is a meaningful and socially relevant interaction model, though the research-platform category is established.
creativity_evidence: The product combines structured political dossiers with direct agent research interaction.
Screenshot presentation visibly emphasizes discover, verify, and compare.
usability_note: The stated natural-language workflow is approachable, but the actual UI was not shown.
red_flags: No submitted video or frame sheets; screenshot is packaging evidence only.
standouts: Evidence-first framing and a high-value civic research use case.
advance_reason: Strong impact and meaningful agent leverage, despite thin execution evidence.

one_line: Runs live agent benchmarks in a browser and preserves comparable experiment records.
what_it_does: Lets users select benchmarks, have an agent start cases and submit answers, and record configurations/results for later comparison.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP makes the agent a first-class benchmark participant with structured case retrieval, answer submission, and PDF access; generic UI driving would be materially less reliable.
leverage_evidence: About text lists start_run, get_next_case, submit_answer, and document-reading tools.
The benchmark judge is fetched from the exact graded commit and run unmodified in-browser.
execution_rationale: The workflow and scope are unusually concrete, with persistent named runs and 15 benchmarks, though frame evidence is not fully inspectable here.
execution_evidence: FACTS report live demo and public repository.
About text specifies a complete run lifecycle and persistent comparison board.
Submitted frame sheets are listed.
impact_rationale: Builders and practitioners have a real recurring need to compare models, prompts, skills, and tools without heavyweight evaluation infrastructure.
impact_evidence: About text states the practical model/prompt/tool selection problem.
Persistent records address regression and reproducibility concerns.
creativity_rationale: Treating a browser benchmark as an exam an existing agent can sit, with exact judge provenance and durable experiment records, is a memorable interaction model.
creativity_evidence: The product frames agent evaluation as a live exam in a browser tab.
Exact-commit judge execution is a distinctive integrity mechanism.
usability_note: No-install/no-login flow and named runs are strong usability choices.
red_flags: No transcript; frame-sheet details are limited.
standouts: Excellent fit between WebMCP and reproducible agent evaluation.
advance_reason: One of the clearest cases where WebMCP changes the product rather than merely adding buttons.

one_line: Durable, editable dashboards that survive recurring workbook refreshes.
what_it_does: Stores source data, recipes, dashboard objects, layout, bindings, provenance, and editions so agents and humans can collaboratively refresh analytics without losing edits.
leverage_rationale: The agent operates on typed native objects and shared persistent workspace state, enabling reliable refresh, provenance, and ambiguity handling that regeneration or UI-driving cannot replicate comparably well.
leverage_evidence: Transcript shows agent inspecting source, drafting cleanup, creating native objects, and saving a recipe.
Transcript describes September refresh resolving renamed headers and escalating an ambiguous missing metric.
About text says human and agent share the same typed command layer and project state.
execution_rationale: The 160-second video transcript demonstrates a coherent end-to-end workflow: source cleanup, native dashboard creation, provenance, human edits, and next-period refresh with ambiguity handling.
execution_evidence: Video transcript explicitly describes August creation and September refresh.
Video frame sheets and named demo video are submitted.
About text enumerates durable objects and month editions.
impact_rationale: Recurring operational reporting is a concrete, costly workflow; preserving human edits while adapting to monthly schema and semantic changes directly addresses the pain.
impact_evidence: Transcript gives realistic changed headers, units, new columns, and missing facility metrics.
About text targets recurring operational reporting and provenance.
creativity_rationale: The durable-dashboard and recipe model reframes generative analytics from disposable output into a living collaborative artifact, pursued deeply through provenance and human approval.
creativity_evidence: Native objects remain editable by humans and discoverable by agents.
Saved transformation recipes and edition history preserve continuity across periods.
usability_note: Shared workspace, direct manipulation, provenance, and explicit ambiguity handling indicate strong usability.
standouts: Strongest demonstrated shared human-agent state and recurring workflow in the packet.
Handles uncertainty instead of silently guessing.
advance_reason: Transformative WebMCP use with unusually strong end-to-end evidence and clear operational value.

one_line: Agent-native vehicle configurator, garage digital twin, owner guide, and 3D creation engine.
what_it_does: Lets agents and humans inspect and revise a fictional vehicle build, control a shared 3D car, measure components, calculate ownership outcomes, and inspect model construction.
leverage_rationale: Deep structured control across five contexts, synchronized 3D state, revision gating, undo, and measurement provenance make the agent a genuine operating layer rather than a UI shortcut.
leverage_evidence: About text reports 49 tools across landing, configurator, garage, guide, and creation engine.
Human interruption, revision-gated mutations, undo, and source/measurement-basis results are specified.
Frame sheets are submitted for the 3D workflow.
execution_rationale: The scope is broad but coherent and backed by a public repo, live demo, and multiple frame sheets; the packet does not provide transcript-level proof of every context.
execution_evidence: FACTS report live demo and public repository.
About text specifies five page contexts and concrete operations.
Frame sheets are listed.
impact_rationale: Car buyers, enthusiasts, and owners can benefit from a shared configurable digital twin and accessible owner guidance, though the fictional vehicle limits immediate real-world reach.
impact_evidence: About text describes configuration, pricing, ownership outcomes, and component guidance.
The product is framed around a shared vehicle model.
creativity_rationale: The combination of agent-operable configurator, synchronized garage twin, visual guide, and measurement-driven 3D creation is highly ambitious and memorable.
creativity_evidence: Four integrated product surfaces plus a creation engine are described.
Agents can reveal and measure 42 named components.
usability_note: Undo, approval gates, and human interruption support safe interaction with a complex 3D workspace.
red_flags: Broad scope creates some uncertainty about completeness of all 49 tools.
advance_reason: Exceptional ambition and leverage with credible implementation evidence.

one_line: Collaborative live what-if decision simulator for humans and AI agents.
what_it_does: Agents create, modify, project, and compare scenarios while users inspect assumptions and consequences in the same live model.
leverage_rationale: Structured scenario mutations and projections let an agent operate on a live decision model precisely instead of returning advice that a user must manually transpose into a spreadsheet.
leverage_evidence: Pitch explicitly lists create, modify, project, and compare WebMCP operations.
About text contrasts direct model operations with manual spreadsheet updates.
execution_rationale: The concept and central workflow are coherent, but there are no submitted video frames and the evidence does not demonstrate a complete scenario run.
execution_evidence: FACTS report a live demo and eight gallery images.
About text describes baseline, alternatives, projections, and comparison.
No frame sheets or transcript submitted.
impact_rationale: People making personal or operational decisions can gain value from inspecting assumptions and comparing alternatives without repetitive spreadsheet work.
impact_evidence: About text describes human constraints/judgment paired with agent modeling work.
The product addresses a clear advice-to-action gap.
creativity_rationale: A live shared decision simulator is a useful and fresh synthesis of agent advice and interactive modeling, though what-if tools are an established category.
creativity_evidence: The human and agent collaboratively manipulate the same live scenarios.
Immediate visible consequences are central to the concept.
usability_note: Inspectable assumptions and immediate projections are promising; actual interface quality is unverified.
red_flags: No submitted video or frame sheets; live demo status alone is insufficient for execution proof.
standouts: Clear bridge from conversational advice to inspectable action.
advance_reason: Strong concept and meaningful WebMCP delta, with execution evidence as the main uncertainty.

one_line: Human-approved AI incident response with prompt-injection-resistant investigation and containment.
what_it_does: Agents investigate incidents, reconstruct attack paths, detect untrusted prompt injection, propose containment, and execute only after explicit approval with an audit trail.
leverage_rationale: Incident response benefits from structured evidence, controlled mutations, approvals, and auditable state; WebMCP enables the agent to investigate and act safely in the operational surface.
leverage_evidence: Pitch explicitly combines investigation, prompt-injection resistance, and approval-gated containment.
Gallery evidence descriptions include compromised-system identification, proposal, approval, isolation, session revocation, and audit saving.
execution_rationale: The packet gives a coherent incident lifecycle and concrete gallery states, but lacks video/transcript and therefore cannot fully prove live execution.
execution_evidence: FACTS report live demo and public repository.
Gallery descriptions enumerate incident overview, injection isolation, approval gate, and completed containment.
No submitted frame sheets or transcript.
impact_rationale: Security teams face a real high-stakes need for faster investigation while preserving human control over destructive actions; the described workflow directly addresses it.
impact_evidence: About text names active incident INC-042 and concrete containment outcomes.
Explicit human approval and audit saving address operational safety.
creativity_rationale: Prompt-injection-resistant incident response with approval-gated execution is an original, timely application of agent-native interaction to a consequential domain.
creativity_evidence: Untrusted evidence is isolated from agent instructions.
Containment is proposed but blocked until approval, then audited.
usability_note: The staged proposal/approval flow is appropriate for high-risk operations.
red_flags: No submitted video or transcript; gallery descriptions are packaging evidence, not direct runtime proof.
standouts: Strong safety model for consequential agent actions.
advance_reason: High impact and leverage with concrete safety-aware workflow evidence.

creativity_rationale: Packaging an AI workspace as a business card may be a new angle, but the submission does not develop or demonstrate it enough to distinguish the concept.
creativity_evidence: Pitch names a workspace/business-card monetization concept.
No interaction model is described.

one_line: Audits storefront agent-readiness and produces evidence-backed fixes and repair CSVs.
what_it_does: Probes a store catalog as a shopping agent would, scores discoverability/data gaps, explains each point against published research, and outputs actionable repairs.
leverage_rationale: Testing the agent-facing catalog surface rather than the human page addresses a distinct machine-readability layer; structured probing and repair output are more reliable than manual inspection.
leverage_evidence: Pitch explicitly contrasts agent retrieval with human-facing theme checkers.
About text describes catalog probing, barcode coverage, receipts, fix lists, and CSV repair.
execution_rationale: The product has a clear audit-to-repair workflow and evidence-backed scoring claims, supported by a live demo, repo, and submitted frame sheets, though no transcript is available.
execution_evidence: FACTS report live demo and public repository.
About text gives concrete audit outputs and field research over 148 storefronts.
Frame sheets are submitted.
impact_rationale: Merchants have a concrete emerging problem: shopping agents cannot reliably read catalogs, causing lost conversions. A diagnostic and repair artifact is directly useful.
impact_evidence: About text reports 148 storefront probes and catalog/barcode failures.
Merchant outputs include score, fix list, receipt, and CSV.
creativity_rationale: The agent-readiness audit reframes commerce SEO around what an agent can retrieve and ties findings to sourced abandonment evidence and repair files.
creativity_evidence: The product evaluates machine-facing catalog access rather than human page appearance.
Every score line is tied to a published table, publisher, and date.
usability_note: Paste-a-domain input with a score and concrete repair artifacts is a strong user flow.
red_flags: Some market statistics in the description are not independently verified within this packet.
standouts: Evidence-backed, actionable bridge from diagnosis to catalog repair.
advance_reason: Clear audience, credible problem, and a differentiated agent-facing audit workflow.

one_line: Discovers and composes capabilities from multiple WebMCP websites for changing user goals.
what_it_does: Helps an agent find providers, compose a plan, adapt when constraints or providers change, and request approval before irreversible actions.
leverage_rationale: Capability discovery and composition across independent WebMCP providers is precisely the structured-agent problem; general UI-driving cannot reliably discover, compose, and recompose these capabilities at comparable quality.
leverage_evidence: Pitch explicitly defines AgentRep as a discovery/composition layer for the agentic web.
About text demonstrates PartyHub, FoodHub, CakeHub, and later PokémonPartyHub composition.
The plan adapts to guest-count and preference changes while preserving valid work.
execution_rationale: The packet gives a concrete multi-provider birthday-planning scenario with changing requirements, budget preservation, and approval, plus public repo/live demo and frame sheets; no transcript lowers certainty.
execution_evidence: FACTS report live demo and public repository.
About text specifies initial three-provider plan, fourth provider discovery, recomposition, and final budget.
Frame sheets are submitted.
impact_rationale: Users and agents need to accomplish goals across sites without knowing providers in advance; adaptive composition has clear practical value for multi-step planning.
impact_evidence: Birthday planning example spans venue, catering, cake, and entertainment.
The agent preserves valid work when requirements change and asks approval before booking.
creativity_rationale: Dynamic discovery of a newly available capability during an active plan, with partial recomposition rather than restart, is a memorable and ambitious interaction model.
creativity_evidence: A fourth provider appears mid-task and is discovered without being named.
Changed guest count invalidates only the affected cake component while the plan remains coherent.
usability_note: Goal-based interaction removes provider-selection burden; approval before booking preserves control.
red_flags: No transcript; multi-provider behavior is claimed in text and frame sheets rather than directly inspectable here.
standouts: Strongest agent-infrastructure concept: discovery, composition, adaptation, and approval in one loop.
advance_reason: Highly differentiated and central WebMCP leverage with a concrete adaptive composition scenario.
